definitions.meaning: Grief, affliction, trouble, evil, calamity, injury

quotations.english: rescued from the popular hate, from calamity

quotations.old_english: He gilleþ geómorlíce and his gyrn sefaþ
quotations.english: mournfully he cries out, sighs forth his grief

quotations.old_english: Gyldaþ nú mid gyrne ðæt heó goda ussa meaht forhogde
quotations.english: requite now with evil her contempt of our gods' might

quotations.old_english: Ðæs ða byre siððan gyrne onguldon
quotations.english: for that the children greviously paid

source_text: gyrn, es; n. Grief, affliction, trouble, evil, calamity, injury :-- Me biþ gyrn witod grief will be appointed me, Exon. 104 b; Th. 396, 18; Rä. 16, 6. Gyrn æfter gomene grief after joy, Beo. Th. 3554; B. 1775. Alýsed of leódhete of gyrme rescued from the popular hate, from calamity, Andr. Kmbl. 2301; An. 1152: 3168; An. 1587. He gilleþ geómorlíce and his gyrn sefaþ mournfully he cries out, sighs forth his grief, Salm. Kmbl. 536; Sat. 267. Gyrn þurh gástgedál affliction through death, Exon. 45 a; Th. 153, 31; Gú. 834. Gyldaþ nú mid gyrne ðæt heó goda ussa meaht forhogde requite now with evil her contempt of our gods' might, 74 b; Th. 279, 25; Jul. 619. Ðæs ða byre siððan gyrne onguldon for that the children greviously paid, 61 b; Th. 226, 23. Wíta unrím grimra gyrna torments numberless, grim troubles, 68 a; Th. 252, 34; Jul. 173: 39 a; Th. 129, 7; Gú. 417. [Cf. O. Sax. gornword.] v. gryn.
